issues.legal_issue: A head lessee whose mining lease survives estate vesting remains a person interested in compensation for the later acquisition of the mining rights, despite having granted a sublease.
material_facts: A long-term mining lease was granted to the claimant, which later granted a sublease over part of the leased land.
The estate vested in the State, after which the mining rights were acquired under the coal-bearing-areas legislation.
The claimant contended that its head-lease interest had survived the estate vesting and that it was entitled to compensation.
issues.conclusion: The claimant’s rights as head lessee survived the estate vesting, and it was a person interested entitled to claim compensation. The High Court’s contrary conclusion was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 4 and 10 of the Bihar Land Reforms Act, 1950, vesting did not extinguish the head lessee’s interest where a subsisting mining lease was deemed to continue under the State; a lessee may retain legal, or mediate, possession through a sublessee. Under Sections 2(d) and 13 of the Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition & Development) Act, 1957, a person claiming an interest in compensation may be a person interested. The Court relied on Bihar Mines Ltd. v. Union of India, 1967 (1) SCR 707, concerning the head lessee’s continuing position after vesting, and Sunder Lal v. Paramsudhdas, concerning the breadth of the expression “person interested.”

predicates.mining_rights_acquisition_compensation_c: A claim for compensation arose from the acquisition of mining rights.
predicates.claimant_held_head_lease: The claimant held the head lease over the mining land.
predicates.head_lease_survived_vesting: The head lease remained in force after the estate vested, even though a sublease had been granted.

issues.definition: When compensation is claimed for acquired mining rights, a claimant holding a head lease that survives vesting is a person interested for compensation.

issues.legal_issue: Reasonable litigation expenses incurred to obtain a mining lease through proceedings for specific performance may be included in compensation for acquired lease rights.
material_facts: The claimant incurred litigation expenses in proceedings to secure specific performance of the agreement to grant the lease.
The tribunal disallowed the litigation-expense claim, and the claimant appealed that disallowance.
The Court found that the litigation could have been necessary to obtain the lease.
issues.conclusion: The litigation-expense claim was allowed as compensation.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13(2)(ii), read with Section 13(1) of the Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition & Development) Act, 1957, permits compensation for reasonable and bona fide expenses of the specified kinds incurred in relation to a lease. The Court held that necessary expenses of prolonged specific-performance litigation to obtain the lease could qualify, consistent with Union of India v. Karanpura Development Co. Ltd., AIR 1976 Pat 121.

predicates.mining_lease_acquisition_compensation_cl: A claimant sought compensation for the acquisition of rights under a mining lease.
predicates.litigation_was_needed_to_obtain_lease: The claimant pursued litigation to secure the lease, and that litigation was necessary to obtain it.
predicates.litigation_expenses_were_reasonable: The litigation expenses were reasonably incurred.

issues.definition: In a claim for compensation for acquired mining lease rights, reasonable expenses of litigation necessary to obtain the lease may be included in compensation.

issues.legal_issue: Expenses reasonably and bona fide incurred by a predecessor in interest to obtain a lease may qualify as a compensation item for a person interested, even if that person did not personally incur them.
material_facts: The claimant had incurred expenses to obtain the lease, while the Court considered whether such expenses could also be claimed by a sublessee who had not incurred them personally.
The Court held that the relevant statutory language did not require the person interested to have personally incurred the expenses.
Because the claimant was held to be a person interested in its own right, the question did not affect the outcome of the appeals.
issues.conclusion: The Court accepted that expenses reasonably and bona fide incurred by a predecessor in interest may qualify, but treated the question as academic in this case.
issues.legal_principle: The Court construed Section 13(1) and Section 13(2) of the Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition & Development) Act, 1957, to require that qualifying expenses be actually, reasonably and bona fide incurred in respect of the land, not necessarily by the person interested personally. Expenses incurred by a predecessor in interest may therefore qualify where there is continuity of title or interest.

predicates.mining_lease_acquisition_compensation_cl: A claimant sought compensation for acquired rights under a mining lease.
predicates.claimant_is_successor_in_interest: The claimant derived its interest in the lease from a predecessor in interest.
predicates.predecessor_reasonably_and_bona_fide_inc: The predecessor reasonably and bona fide incurred expenses to obtain the lease.

issues.definition: In compensation claims for acquired mining lease rights, qualifying expenses incurred by a predecessor may be claimed by a successor in interest.

issues.legal_issue: A claim for solatium is not allowable where the acquisition does not involve sustaining the operation of the mining lease.
material_facts: The claimant sought solatium in addition to compensation for acquired mining lease rights.
The Court found that there was no question of sustaining the operation of the mining lease in the circumstances of the claim.
issues.conclusion: The claim for solatium was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the claim under Section 13(4) of the Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition & Development) Act, 1957, was unsupported because the circumstances did not involve sustaining the operation of the mining lease.

predicates.mining_lease_acquisition_compensation_cl: The proceeding concerns compensation for acquired rights under a mining lease.
predicates.solatium_claimed: The claimant requested solatium in addition to other compensation.
predicates.mining_operation_sustenance_not_at_issue: The acquisition claim did not involve sustaining the operation of the mining lease.

issues.definition: When solatium is claimed in a mining-lease acquisition compensation proceeding that does not involve sustaining the lease’s operation, solatium is not allowable.
